purpose: Author the refrigeration shop guide from its operation records and schematic drawing primitives.
title: Refrigeration bench guide
subtitle: Coil fabrication, sealed-system work, leak checks and loaded commissioning

extra.qualification_scope: Manual sequence and source review; records no completed circuit build, charge or load test

pages.title: Build the cold loop
pages.subtitle: Wind the evaporator, transfer the donor circuit, and prove the installed refrigeration assembly.

actions.title: Identify and prepare the core
actions.body: Identify the donor on page 2. Prepare and inspect the core on pages 3-8. Support and trace the sealed donor on pages 9 and 10.

actions.title: Join and prove the circuit
actions.body: Recovery, open work, leak testing and weighing are on pages 11-26. Install the hardware and controls before the powered tests.

actions.title: Read the bench cards
actions.body: First run starts on page 33. The leak-route map, pressure-temperature card and charge decisions follow. Jump by task using PDF bookmarks.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Finish each recorded check in order. The unit record keeps the actual readings and joint evidence.

pages.title: Identify the Antarctic Star donor
pages.subtitle: Match the selected ice maker to its U.S. certification report and record the actual hardware.

drawing.value: No charge mass on inspected plate.
The certification rating supplies the first weighed trial.

actions.title: Record the actual assembly
actions.body: Photograph the appliance and compressor labels. Log the model, supply and compressor identity. Match the condenser, fan, capillary and mount interfaces to the reference.

actions.title: Use the U.S. certification rating
actions.body: Intertek lists the HZB-12/Q at 115 V / 60 Hz with 16 g of R600a. The inspected appliance label gives no mass. Enter the report as the baseline source.

actions.title: Record the leads before harvest
actions.body: Retain the compressor terminal cover. Trace the factory-external leads, termination and earth point for this unit before fabricating the matching harness.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The donor identity and R600a rating are established. The first trial is 16.0 g by net delivered mass.

pages.title: Reserve both coil tails
pages.subtitle: Cut the dry coil stock with a tubing cutter, with enough copper for the wrap and each separate routed tail.

drawing.value: INLET / shell exit is the datum
OUTLET / shell exit is the datum

actions.title: Use the specified stock
actions.body: GOORY ACR copper, 1/4 in OD x 0.031 in wall. Keep its bore clean and capped. Do not saw refrigerant tubing.

actions.title: Mark the wrap and tails
actions.body: Cut to the stock length on EVAP-01. Mark the winding and both allowances from the finished form.

actions.title: Keep the allowances intact
actions.body: Each allowance includes the in-shell route and protrusion. The longer outlet route still leaves the shorter outside working length.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The two tails are labeled and the ends are round, square, burr-free and protected from dirt.

pages.title: Wind the copper coil
pages.subtitle: Use the printed mandrel groove to place a single layer of tubing without flattening the bore.

drawing.value: Keep the tube in its groove
Mark the inlet at the entry
The groove rough-forms the copper. Finish the winding on the vessel.

actions.title: Register the inlet allowance
actions.body: Mark the inlet tail on the straight stock. Seat the start of the winding in the groove and keep the allowance free where the groove begins.

actions.title: Rough-form in the printed groove
actions.body: Support the free tube as it feeds. Keep each new wrap seated without flattening or crossing the previous turn. Leave both working tails straight and capped.

actions.title: Check the released form
actions.body: Slide axially off the mandrel. Inspect for flattened spots, creases and crossed turns. Set the final turn count and tail clocking on the vessel.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The winding slips off as one layer. Both working tails are clear and uncreased.

pages.title: Dress the bare wall
pages.subtitle: Prove the rim bond, steel contact and reed crossings before covering them.

drawing.value: Use the rim bond, wall probe and reed crossings before covering the steel.

actions.title: Fit and prove the rim earth bond
actions.body: Fasten the ring against bare upper-rim steel. Support the lead with the crimp pointing up and leave it free for the lid. Measure from bare vessel to the free earth lead. Subtract meter lead resistance.

actions.title: Tape the wall probe to bare steel
actions.body: Fit the DS18B20 flat face in the west-side winding gap opposite the reed bridge. Keep its insulated leads in that gap until they turn up.

actions.title: Locate the reed bridge from the float
actions.body: Set the bridge with its calibrated gauge. Check rising CHI and falling CLO over three sweeps at nominal and greatest float retreat. Require no missed crossings and spread within 2 mm.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Rim bond, wall probe and both reed transitions are recorded with the surfaces still accessible.

pages.title: Transfer and bond the coil
pages.subtitle: Foil the vessel, ease the coil into position and bond the freeze probe to the suction end.

drawing.value: Bare steel in the winding gap
The contact points are exposed here. Dress both with foil in the actual core.

actions.title: Foil and transfer without shifting contacts
actions.body: Apply continuous 3M 425 foil where the copper contacts steel. Ease the winding onto the vessel. Lift the wrap around the reed bridge without pressing it onto the reeds.

actions.title: Bond the copper probe
actions.body: Tape the DS18S20 flat against the last, upper turn before the suction tail. Lead the bus from the coil probe to the steel probe. Keep both in firm contact under the foil.

actions.title: Identify both live sensors before foam
actions.body: Power the low-voltage reader and run thermal. The wall probe is 0x28 and the coil probe 0x10. Warm each contact gently in turn and confirm the expected channel moves.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Both actual probes report under their own family code and respond at the intended contact.

pages.title: Route the two exits
pages.subtitle: Clock the upper and lower tails before the vessel is fully seated in the open shell.

drawing.value: Measure on the real routed part

actions.title: Follow the coil turns to tag each tail
actions.body: The bottom turn feeds E1 at Y -77.50. The top suction turn leaves at E2, Y +77.50. Both exits point out the -X face of the shell.

actions.title: Support each tail as the vessel drops
actions.body: Feed the supported tubes through the holes in stages. Inspect for flattening at the turns, shell mouths and bends. Burnish the foil collars into place.

actions.title: Measure from the outer face
actions.body: Measure along each exposed straight from the shell face to the untrimmed end. E1 is 200 to 205 mm and E2 is 175 to 180 mm. Protect the open ends.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Both outside working lengths and the pre-pour collar seal are visible and recorded.

pages.title: Inspect the core before foam
pages.subtitle: Catch a moved reed, floating probe or open collar while the parts can still be reached.

drawing.value: Shell face is the length datum
The copper ends here mark the exits. Use the prior page for the working lengths.

actions.title: Inspect from inside and outside
actions.body: Use a lamp along both tube mouths. Look for a lifted foil edge, gap into the foam cavity, trapped lead or kink. Keep the bore capped and inserts clear.

actions.title: Prove the buried functions
actions.body: Read thermal and prove both sensor responses. Verify both float crossings and the steel-to-lead resistance. Photograph each sensor contact and both collars.

actions.title: Complete the cold-core pour
actions.body: Keep the reed and service paths dry. Follow the cold-core assembly for mask, pour and cure. At handoff verify a cured shell, intact seals and free copper exits.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Both probes, reed crossings, earth bond, tail clocking and foil collars are recorded.

pages.source: Cold-core assembly / EVAP-01 / coil assembly numbers

pages.title: Support before teardown
pages.subtitle: Remove only the donor casing and supports that prevent access, while keeping the sealed circuit undamaged.

drawing.value: Lines carry refrigerant, not the assembly's weight.

actions.title: Unplug and identify the leads
actions.body: Keep mains isolated. Photograph the factory-external compressor and fan connections. Retain the terminal/PTC cover and its original retention.

actions.title: Support each body
actions.body: Keep the compressor upright. Support the condenser, fan and evaporator before undoing their fasteners. Copper tubing must not hold their weight.

actions.title: Preserve the useful details
actions.body: Record the factory external leads and terminal cover. Keep each body supported. Trace and tag the sealed tubing on the next page.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: A missing, cracked, altered or loose terminal cover fails the assembly before power is applied.

pages.title: Trace and tag the donor circuit
pages.subtitle: Identify the retained components and mark each separation while the donor is intact.

actions.title: Trace the retained loop
actions.body: Follow compressor discharge to condenser, drier and capillary. Follow the evaporator outlet back to suction. Tag the parts of the bonded capillary/suction pair.

actions.title: Mark the branches on the actual donor
actions.body: Tag both ends of the finger plate, then trace the harvest solenoid line back to its discharge tee. Photograph all three locations before recovery.

actions.title: Protect the factory drier and capillary
actions.body: Keep the drier, capillary, terminal helix and bonded section intact. Identify the factory process stub at the compressor for the service plan.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The two evaporator separations and the discharge-side bypass branch are identified.

pages.title: Stage the refrigeration bench
pages.subtitle: Lay out the instruments by the measurement or service task they actually perform.

drawing.value: Cylinder and valve mass. Support the hose off the pan.
AMP and WATT at the bench supply. Log whole-unit draw.
thermal / status. Wall 0x28 and suction-end coil 0x10.
De-energized localization after A3 area clearance.
Recovery set, dry gas, rated manifold, micron gauge,
sealed access and qualified charged-circuit detector.
Low-volume pressure points, contact probes and
an immersion probe for a delivered-water measurement.

actions.title: Check the instrument markings at the bench
actions.body: The Orion A/C set and modeled BPV31 have no documented R600a approval here. Use fittings, gauges, pump and recovery gear specified for the actual A3 service.

actions.title: Write down the service boundary
actions.body: List who provides each service device, where its gauge reads, the circuit test-pressure limit and the way the process tube will be sealed before opening the donor.

actions.title: Set up the work area and isolation
actions.body: Keep ignition sources out. Set up ventilation and the safe disconnect. Prepare and check the ambient and joint detectors on the next page before recovery.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The table assigns each needed instrument and names the service method before opening.

pages.source: Tool ledger / Secop hermetic service / Whirlpool A3 service

pages.title: Set up the detector
pages.subtitle: Separate the shop locator from the technician’s charged-circuit detector and ambient monitor.

drawing.value: Cool, power isolated and area already cleared.
Use to locate an indication after clearance.
In clean air wait 30 s for two beeps. High, sound on.
Sweep at 1 to 5 cm. Clear for 10 to 30 s in clean air.
Start in clean air on Max. Wait for a steady beep,
usually 30 s to 2 min. Use its specified batteries.
Check response to the R600a reference, then clear.
Move 25 to 50 mm/s, close without touching.
Keep the separate detector on at the low point.
Record clearance and stop the work for an alarm.

actions.title: Prove the response before sweeping
actions.body: With the GAS-Mate setup, use the specified batteries and wait for a steady baseline. Check against the known R600a reference before and after joint sweeps. Return to clean air between checks.

actions.title: Use the owned locator within its instructions
actions.body: The owned TopTes uses fresh AAA batteries. Leave High and sound on for cool, isolated checks after clearance. Check the auto-off setting. Bars show relative response.

actions.title: Keep area and joint checks distinct
actions.body: Keep a separate A3 ambient monitor running low near the work. Use the charged-circuit wand for the following pressure-state checks. Record instrument and reference response.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Area monitor is running. The charged-circuit instrument responds to the known R600a source.

pages.source: TopTes PT520A manual / INFICON GAS-Mate operating instructions

pages.title: Recover the factory charge
pages.subtitle: Recover R600a into a suitable cylinder before cold-opening the circuit.

drawing.value: Locate the actual dead-end stub above the suction return.
The model marks the station. Connect the qualified recovery set to the actual stub.

actions.title: Identify the actual stub
actions.body: Isolate the donor at its supply. Follow the short dead-end process tube on the compressor. The pinch and factory seal distinguish it from the suction and discharge lines.

actions.title: Recover through the specified service connection
actions.body: An A3 technician connects the approved recovery set and cylinder in the cleared work area. Record removed mass, component identity and the recovery check.

actions.title: Clear retained refrigerant
actions.body: The technician verifies circuit and oil clearance by the approved service method before a tube is cut or heated. Record the actual measurement and equipment used.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Factory gas is recovered, power isolated and residual refrigerant clearance is recorded.

pages.title: Prove the inert sweep before heat
pages.subtitle: Use an open outlet and prove flow through the segment that is about to be heated.

drawing.value: Verify this path independently through its actual inlet and outlet.
Recheck the flow whenever a cut, coupling or valve changes the route.
A regulator reading shows supply pressure. Check gas at the free outlet.

actions.title: Stage dry gas and regulator
actions.body: Have the technician identify the dry gas and regulator combination. Keep the drier dry. Complete recovery and circuit clearance before cold-opening any line.

actions.title: Prove flow across the actual joint
actions.body: Identify the gas inlet, tube segment and open exit. Check flow at the exit before each braze. Verify the discharge and capillary path independently from the suction path.

actions.title: Recheck before making the second joint
actions.body: Joining one end changes the gas route. Establish a safe open exit for the next joint, confirm it flows and keep the setup in its cleared, ventilated work area.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: A verified open inert flow path crosses each heated joint when that joint is made.

pages.title: Cut at the evaporator
pages.subtitle: Separate the finger plate after recovery. Preserve the entire original metering path.

drawing.value: Keep this length and bonded pair
Free the finger plate from these two joins.
Separate the bypass at its own junction.
Prove the open outlet at each heated joint.

actions.title: Cold-cut the old evaporator outlet
actions.body: Support both sides. Use the tube cutter close to the old plate on the return line and preserve the donor suction length needed for the coupling.

actions.title: Cold-cut the capillary at the plate inlet
actions.body: Use the Mastercool capillary cutter. Keep the retained end round and clear. Preserve the original working length, terminal helix and bonded section.

actions.title: Remove the freed finger plate
actions.body: Support it as the cuts release it. Complete the bypass separation on page 16 before taking the assembly apart. Protect the retained openings from debris.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Both cuts keep the donor capillary, its bonded section and the drier intact.

pages.title: Remove the hot-gas branch
pages.subtitle: The harvest line connects to the retained discharge path upstream of the condenser.

drawing.value: Verify the retained discharge route after separation.
The diagram traces the branch. Use the actual junction and materials for the join.

actions.title: Trace the non-metered line
actions.body: Follow the solenoid tube from the old finger plate to its discharge junction. Record the physical junction and tube material while the retained compressor/condenser route is visible.

actions.title: Establish the separation and rejoin
actions.body: The A3 service plan identifies how the branch and tee come out while leaving a sealed discharge route. Confirm the actual join and its inert path before opening the junction.

actions.title: Inspect the retained discharge run
actions.body: Check the remaining line is supported, unobstructed and clear of the frame. Mark any new joint for the pressure test and charged sweep.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The retained discharge path reaches the condenser and every new joint is logged.

pages.title: Set up pressure and tube probes
pages.subtitle: Place probes where each reading answers a specific question before closing the circuit.

drawing.value: Evaporator outlet superheat before the bonded run.
Vapor margin entering the compressor after that run.
Subcooling upstream of the drier. Pair pressure and tube T.
Mark the process/access location on the actual circuit before pressure testing.

actions.title: Clamp on clean copper
actions.body: Fit insulated contact probes to bare copper at A and B. Mark the sensor leads. A is immediately after the coil and B is near compressor suction. Log the probe accuracy.

actions.title: Plan pressure access before sealing
actions.body: Confirm which fitted port represents B. If diagnosing feed, provide rated local C pressure access during the decharged build. Add local A access if outlet superheat is needed.

actions.title: Label values from a shared tap
actions.body: B pressure with A temperature gives apparent outlet superheat and can bias it high. Keep mass and volume of the running test connections consistent across trials.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The log identifies each temperature and pressure separately, with its actual reading location.

pages.title: Wet rag on each stub
pages.subtitle: Both joints sit on copper that runs back into a PET-GF shell with cured foam behind it. Protect it before each braze.

drawing.value: Flame / hot gas away from core

actions.title: Set a water-wet heat sink
actions.body: Soak a clean cotton rag. Wring it until wet without dripping. Place it on the shell side of the upcoming joint with the bore and joint kept dry.

actions.title: Seat and aim
actions.body: Press the rag around the tube at the shell exit. Keep it against the exit collar. Support the joint and direct flame and exhaust away from plastic and foam.

actions.title: Inspect after every heated joint
actions.body: After cooling, remove the rag in place. Check the collar and shell for gloss, sag, dimples, lifted foil or scorching. Stage a fresh wet rag for the next braze.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Both shell exits retain their shape and seal after the joints cool.

pages.title: Braze the suction coupling
pages.subtitle: Join the upper outlet to factory suction with the ACR slip coupling and a proved inert sweep.

drawing.value: Clean sockets / full intended engagement / no stress

actions.title: Inspect the dry fit
actions.body: Clean both tube ends and the slip socket. Mark insertion depth on both ends and center the sleeve over both ends without spring load.

actions.title: Set purge and heat protection
actions.body: Prove the actual inert outlet. Fit the wet rag at the shell exit on page 18. Keep the coupling clear of water and the heated path clear of foam.

actions.title: Inspect the cooled joints
actions.body: Use BCuP-5 on the copper joint. After the joint cools, check the full ring at each sleeve mouth and the tube support. Record both seams for pressure testing.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Both sleeve mouths and the shell exit pass visual inspection. Pressure testing follows.

pages.title: Pinch-swage the capillary
pages.subtitle: Form the inlet stub around the retained capillary, then braze with a proved open sweep.

drawing.value: Form the 1/4 in outer stub around the retained capillary.

actions.title: Dry-fit the uncrushed metering end
actions.body: Align the capillary with the E1 stub. Inspect the capillary tip before inserting it. Mark the dry fit so the capillary remains at its intended position during forming.

actions.title: Form the outer tube with smooth jaws
actions.body: Use the Knipex 86 01 180 on the outer stub. Work around the circumference in 60 degree increments. Check the capillary bore and flow path before heating.

actions.title: Braze under the proved dry sweep
actions.body: Stage a fresh wet rag and verify the outlet path across this joint. Inspect the cooled swage, tube alignment and shell exit. Log the seam for the pressure test.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The original metering length and clear flow path are retained. Record the cooled swage.

pages.title: Pressure-test the inert circuit
pages.subtitle: Use the approved shop pressure for the complete connected circuit. Check the joints while the charge is still dry gas.

drawing.value: FILL, ISOLATE AND READ ON THE CIRCUIT SIDE
Gas, regulated pressure, fixture and rated circuit limits.
Circuit pressure, gas/tube temperature, time and bubbles.

actions.title: Document the approved set pressure
actions.body: Intertek lists 88 psig for the donor low side. The approved connected-loop pressure and hold must respect that rating and any lower limits of the rebuilt circuit and test fixture.

actions.title: Isolate and wait for temperatures to settle
actions.body: Read the gauge connected to the circuit. Allow both sides to equalize through the capillary. Record pressure, temperature and time once stable, then at the end of the hold.

actions.title: Inspect with leak-detection solution
actions.body: Brush approved solution around every seam on the positively pressurized inert circuit. Watch for bubbles that grow. Record the location, then clean and dry before evacuating.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Log the approved pressure and hold result. Repair any bubble growth or unexplained loss.

pages.title: Pull vacuum and isolate the pump
pages.subtitle: Read absolute pressure at the circuit while pumping and while the pump is isolated.

drawing.value: 15 min at target with pump connected
Then isolate the pump and log 15 min.

actions.title: Connect after releasing the inert test gas
actions.body: Connect the A3 vacuum set with the micron gauge on the circuit side of the isolation valve. Include the high side in the approved setup and allow it time to evacuate.

actions.title: Start the pumping timer at the target
actions.body: Reach 500 microns or below at the circuit. Keep pumping at least 15 minutes from that point. Record the lowest stable reading and the setup.

actions.title: Isolate the pump and read the hold
actions.body: Leave the micron gauge connected to the circuit. Record at isolation and 15 minutes later. Have the technician resolve a sustained rise before charging.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Record actual micron readings under pump and after isolation, alongside the pressure test.

pages.title: Meter the recharge
pages.subtitle: Deliver 16.0 g of R600a into the evacuated loop for the first instrumented trial.

drawing.value: Account for hose and valve inventory

actions.title: Set the scale and isolate the loop
actions.body: After pressure test and vacuum, check the Smart Weigh scale with a known small mass on the supported cylinder setup. Keep hoses clear of the pan.

actions.title: Deliver a known first charge
actions.body: Use the approved low-volume A3 set and transfer method with the compressor stopped. Aim for 16.0 g past the isolation valve. Record the mass and fixture states.

actions.title: Check the delivered amount
actions.body: Subtract any increase in trapped fixture mass and any amount routed elsewhere. Use page 24 to complete the transfer record before starting the compressor.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Record the net delivered mass and its uncertainty before first start.

pages.title: Account for one gram
pages.subtitle: The isolation valve is the boundary between delivered refrigerant and refrigerant still in the service set.

drawing.value: Record both fixture states. A liquid heel and vapor can share one pressure.
At 40 C, 2 mL holds about 1.06 g as liquid or 0.027 g as saturated vapor.

actions.title: Prove scale repeatability under load
actions.body: Support the hose without pulling on the scale. Remove and replace a known check mass near 1 g several times in the loaded position. Record its indicated change and spread.

actions.title: Use a known fixture inventory
actions.body: Use the specified metered transfer setup or measure the small isolated inventory change. Count recovered fixture liquid in that term once. Log all grams leaving elsewhere.

actions.title: Resolve uncertainty before tuning
actions.body: Require delivered-mass uncertainty within 0.25 g to interpret a 1.0 g move. If the amount is uncertain or must come down, recover and weigh a new known total.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The worksheet records cylinder loss, fixture change, diverted mass and net grams.

pages.source: Refrigerant-loop §8 / Smart Weigh Pro / NIST phase densities

pages.title: Estimate the running coil inventory
pages.subtitle: Use the tube bore and phase distribution to estimate the mass held by the wrapped coil.

drawing.value: ILLUSTRATIVE RUNNING INVENTORY IN THE NEW COIL
-10 C evaporation  /  30 C liquid-equivalent capillary inlet
At -20 to -5 C evaporating and 20-35 C liquid equivalent, the models give 0.3-2.2 g.
NET CHANGE = NEW COIL - REMOVED PARTS + RETAINED INVENTORY CHANGE
At 40 C, about 2 mL more liquid in the condenser shifts about 1 g.

actions.title: Use the bore volume
actions.body: Use 4.78 mm bore and the actual trimmed length. For the example, 26% of the inlet mass has flashed. Vapor quality rises linearly to dryout at 90% of the winding.

actions.title: Subtract what came out
actions.body: The finger plate and hot-gas branch carried refrigerant. If the removed plate is measured, keep the recovered, isolated scrap separate from the retained circuit.

actions.title: Keep the largest unknown visible
actions.body: Phase distribution in the retained condenser and drier, and refrigerant dissolved in oil, can move the total by grams. These cases illustrate the coil contribution.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The certification rating supplies the first fill. The loaded test determines the operating fill.

pages.source: EVAP-01 / NIST isobutane data / ORNL void-fraction models

pages.title: Isolate the service set
pages.subtitle: Close the charge path and retain only the agreed running measurement fixture.

drawing.value: Log net grams for this trial

actions.title: Close at the marked circuit boundary
actions.body: Close the circuit isolation valve. Recover trapped gas in the attached A3 set before disconnecting. Keep the qualified low-volume running pressure fixture in its intended position.

actions.title: Check access and closure
actions.body: Cap disconnected ports. Include the access body and threads in the pressure and charged checks. Plan a final sealed closure and its recheck after tuning.

actions.title: Transfer the data to the run log
actions.body: Record net grams, uncertainty, the fitted instruments, and any volume left attached for the run. Keep the setup the same for comparison.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: Every charge path is isolated and recording points for the run are identified.

pages.title: Place the gas sensor first
pages.subtitle: Install the MQ-6 in the open floor strip before the compressor makes the slot hard to reach.

drawing.value: Seat the card low and keep the path along the floor open.

actions.title: Identify mesh and header
actions.body: On the sensor card, distinguish the mesh face from its wire header. Orient the mesh west into the floor wall well and the header east into the open bay.

actions.title: Check the two retaining grooves
actions.body: Lower the board straight to the shoulders. Tug the loom lightly and confirm the board stays seated. Keep the low route between the joints and sensor open.

actions.title: Prove the installed interlock
actions.body: Run the approved gas-interlock commissioning test and record actual relay dropout. Use the A3 bench ambient monitor during service work.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Mesh, cable clearance and retention are visible. Record actual interlock behavior before start.

pages.title: Lower the compressor
pages.subtitle: Mount the connected refrigeration assembly without transferring its weight into the copper lines.

drawing.value: Align the four openings before the weight is lowered.
Seat the washers squarely and check the real compression and clearance.

actions.title: Lower onto all grommets evenly
actions.body: Support the cold core and condenser separately. Face the intact terminal cover forward and align all posts through their grommets before bringing down the plate.

actions.title: Stack washer, rubber and post
actions.body: Use the M5 x 10 screws with OD25 fender washers. Confirm the insert stays square and the washer is centered over the rubber and post. Seat the stack at the post crown.

actions.title: Check the plate and tubes by hand
actions.body: Confirm no rocking or hard plate-to-floor contact. The rubber stays seated and supported. Check both copper paths move without rubbing when the plate shifts slightly on its rubber.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The posts, washers and grommets carry the compressor. The copper stays clear and relaxed.

pages.title: Seat the condenser and fan
pages.subtitle: Use the printed rails and aft fingers to carry the condenser block above the slab.

drawing.value: Seat the front flanges in the rails and secure both aft flange holes.

actions.title: Seat the block in its rails
actions.body: Support the condenser and slide the front flanges into the rail grooves while the aft tabs land on the printed fingers. Both sides must reach their seats before tightening.

actions.title: Secure both aft flanges
actions.body: Use the two M3 x 8 screws into the fingers. Reach the lower screw from aft while the bay is open. Check that the fin block cannot shift or distort.

actions.title: Check the air path under power
actions.body: During the fan check, use a paper strip outside each grille and record which pulls and which blows. Keep the strip clear of the blades. Trace dislodged wires or obstructions.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Both mounts are seated and actual through-flow is recorded at the two grilles.

pages.title: Seat the thermal cutoff
pages.subtitle: The 77 C one-shot fuse reads through contact with the outside flank of the retained donor power cover.

drawing.value: The clamp and cover move with the compressor. Prove the installed fit.

actions.title: Seat the fuse casing against the cover
actions.body: The case lies in the clamp channel on the +X flank. Keep the first 3 mm of both leads straight as they leave the case. Insulate leads and crimp connections.

actions.title: Engage both leaves in their slot
actions.body: Slide the leaves between the retained power-box cover and the compressor mounting plate. The clamp rides with the compressor clear of the enclosure.

actions.title: Inspect retention and electrical separation
actions.body: Without power, tug the strain-relieved leads gently and confirm the fuse case stays seated. Check clearance to bare compressor metal and continuity per the AC schedule.

result.title: HOLD
result.body: Record case seating, clamp retention, lead clearance and insulation at the actual assembly.

pages.title: Prove the controls before first start
pages.subtitle: Use the actual probes and fan on the wired appliance. Check the relays from the console.

actions.title: Return to actual sensor readings
actions.body: Send sim off. Run thermal and confirm wall device 0x28 and coil device 0x10. Use status to read both values, the cold state and the relay request.

actions.title: Check fan and electrical protection
actions.body: Inspect earth continuity, the donor terminal cover and fuse clamp before power. Use selftest in the cleared setup and confirm the condenser fan physically moves air.

actions.title: Check the ready state
actions.body: Record gas clear and the installed interlock test. Let the normal 3 min minimum-off timer finish. A warm wall above the 4 C call point can then start the loop.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The actual temperature channels, airflow, interlock and restart protection have been proved.

pages.source: Shipping firmware / actual probes and fan control

pages.title: Check the condenser air path
pages.subtitle: Use the real fan to prove air enters one side and exits the opposite side.

drawing.value: Use a light strip outside each grille. Keep it clear of the rotor.

actions.title: Inspect with the unit isolated
actions.body: Look through the grille and fin path. Seat all mounts, keep the wire loom clear, and confirm the copper can’t rub fins, rails or a spinning fan.

actions.title: Prove the actual direction
actions.body: During the cleared fan test, hold a light strip outside the intake and exhaust grilles. It should pull at the west grille and blow at the east grille.

actions.title: Check again at the first cold call
actions.body: Watch the actual airflow when the compressor starts with the normal controls. Correct a stalled fan, reversed flow or an obstructed grille before loaded trials.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Both grilles pass the movement check and the supply and exhaust stay clear.

pages.source: Condenser block / electrical commissioning / shipping fan control

pages.title: Read the first powered run
pages.subtitle: Observe a normal start with the mounted components, real sensors and electrical protections active.

drawing.value: Wall C / coil C, RMS A / W,
Record whole-feed readings. Treat the first good trace as the comparison.

actions.title: Start with normal demand
actions.body: Set the P4400 on the protected feed outside the service area. Take standby readings. When the warm wall calls after the off guard, watch the fan and compressor.

actions.title: Measure the short run
actions.body: Press AMP to read running RMS amps and WATT/VA until W appears. Use thermal or status for the coil trend. Log both readings and which other loads were on.

actions.title: End the test safely
actions.body: End the brief run at 60 s or sooner for stalled hum, overload, no airflow, a guard trip or an alarm. Use the safe bench disconnect. Leave the restart delay in force.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The relay, fan, running draw and fall in coil temperature are recorded as a baseline.

pages.source: P3 Kill A Watt P4400 manual / firmware-and-commissioning.md

pages.title: Sweep the actual joint seams
pages.subtitle: Pass the tip slowly around each joint and repeat a local response only after the area is clear.

drawing.value: Keep the sensor close and move at the detector’s specified sweep rate.
A response that returns at one seam is a leak indication.

actions.title: Plan the sweep with the bay open
actions.body: Use the joint map on the next page. Include both ends of the suction sleeve, each factory connection and any new discharge work. Sweep the exposed seam all the way around.

actions.title: Move close and slowly
actions.body: With GAS-Mate, scan at 25 to 50 mm/s around the seam and underside. Keep the tip close without touching hot copper, blades or terminals. Maintain the service ventilation.

actions.title: Handle a response without obscuring it
actions.body: For a local response, pause the trial, withdraw to clean air and let the instrument recover. Recheck only after area clearance. Log any repeatable response and stop for repair.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Every accessible logged seam has been swept at its appropriate pressure state.

pages.source: Secop hermetic service §3.4 / detector manufacturer instructions

pages.title: Locate the joints on the machine
pages.subtitle: Use the installed model to orient the joint list before looking at the actual brazes and service seals.

drawing.value: Check the factory and rebuilt joints.
Inspect the actual seams at the tails.
The CAD views locate the runs. Mark and sweep the physical connections.

actions.title: Walk the high side from the compressor
actions.body: Start where discharge leaves the can. Follow it into the condenser and through both drier joints to the capillary feed. Include any new discharge connection.

actions.title: Find both new connections at the shell
actions.body: At E1 follow the capillary into the inlet swage. At E2 follow the outlet into the suction sleeve. Mark both sleeve mouths as separate seams.

actions.title: Finish the return and access checks
actions.body: Follow suction back to the can, then locate the process connection above it. Include all fixture seals, accessible factory connections and the final closure.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The work record names each physical seam and keeps any blocked location visible.

pages.title: Find the high and low seams
pages.subtitle: Check the exposed joints in the running and stopped states that can reveal a leak.

drawing.value: Discharge stub, all new discharge seams, condenser
U-bends and headers, drier ends and capillary feed.
E1 swage, both E2 coupling seams, suction stub, process
tap body, core and cap, plus any instrument connections.
The final low-side seal and disturbed joints. Confirm
positive pressure for the electronic joint sweep.
The earlier inert test covers the complete circuit, including the buried coil.
Mark every exposed joint where the installed model and physical unit differ.

actions.title: Sweep the pressure side on the running check
actions.body: After first start, use a normal on-cycle for the high-side sweep. Keep the guards and fan active. Cover discharge, condenser, drier and every seam in that pressure state.

actions.title: Stop and prove positive low-side pressure
actions.body: Stop and let the sides equalize. Low-side pressure must exceed ambient by more than gauge uncertainty. Otherwise record the charged check as inconclusive and use the inert test.

actions.title: Recheck after disturbing the access
actions.body: Repeat the relevant checks after disconnecting and capping, then at final closure and after the loaded cycle. Record each area with pressure state and result.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: High-side and positive low-side sweeps are logged. Any unresolved indication stops release.

pages.title: Stop on a detector alarm
pages.subtitle: Power isolation and area clearance take priority over finding the exact joint.

drawing.value: Withdraw. Use the protected remote disconnect and
approved ventilation from outside the affected area.
Tag the joint from the work record and recover before
reopening it. Repeat inert, vacuum and charged checks.
Record the charged sweep as inconclusive for that
side. Use the documented inert test for that path.
Record pressure state, instrument and reference check.
Complete the final closure check after tuning.

actions.title: Leave switching outside the affected area
actions.body: Use the bench disconnect from the safe area. Return only under the A3 clearance procedure. Keep ordinary electrical controls in the affected area untouched.

actions.title: Distinguish a local peak from background
actions.body: Recheck the instrument with the known source. A repeatable local peak is repair work. A broad response calls for area clearance, then a repeat search.

actions.title: Use the repair sequence
actions.body: Record the joint and the state in which it was found. Recovery, gas clearance, repair, inert test, vacuum and a new weighed charge precede further operation.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The bench record identifies each alarm or unresolved joint and its disposition.

pages.source: Whirlpool A3 service / Secop hermetic service

pages.title: Repeat the same pull-down window
pages.subtitle: Time the built-in wall reading through the same interval with the normal water load and airflow.

drawing.value: Time, wall C, coil C, cold state, live A and W.
Pressure and tube temperatures at the fitted points.

actions.title: Reset to the same fill and starting temperature
actions.body: Use the same high-reed fill and match the beginning wall and supply-water readings near ambient. Keep the enclosure, fan and inlet conditions the same. Log the inlet air if measured.

actions.title: Keep the load fixed while it pulls down
actions.body: Pause draws and refills during the comparison window. Keep normal guards active. Read status every 30 s and stamp the first wall readings at or below 12 C and 8 C.

actions.title: Compare the time and the conditions
actions.body: Record the 12 to 8 C elapsed time with net grams and the coil trend. If a guard ends the run early, record which one. A wall trace compares runs through the same setup.

actions.title: Check the finished cold end
actions.body: Record the last on-cycle readings and a normal restart. For refrigerant diagnosis, pair the pressure and tube readings at the points on page 17.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Record wall pull-down time, inlet conditions, charge and cold-end behavior for each trial.

pages.title: Look up R600a saturation
pages.subtitle: Use absolute pressure from the matching measurement location and interpolate between rows.

drawing.value: Absolute pressure = signed gauge pressure + measured local air pressure.

actions.title: Convert the gauge reading
actions.body: Example with measured station pressure of 14.36 psia: -1.44 psig gives 12.92 psia. The table puts saturation near -15 C. An absolute instrument gives the table input directly.

actions.title: Calculate suction superheat
actions.body: Subtract saturation from the tube temperature at the same point. At 12.92 psia and a tube at -7 C, superheat is 8 K. Near -15 C, 1 psi pressure error costs about 1.9 K.

actions.title: Calculate condenser outlet subcooling
actions.body: At 531.2 kPa absolute, saturation is 40 C. A nearby liquid-line temperature of 36 C gives 4 K subcooling. Record measured values and the uncertainty.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The table supplies saturation temperatures for measured pressures. Find limits in the service plan.

pages.source: NIST Chemistry WebBook SRD 69 / R600a saturation

pages.title: Measure the water in the glass
pages.subtitle: Read actual dispensed water temperature at a repeatable point in the pour sequence.

drawing.value: Keep the tip clear of glass.

actions.title: Set up the thermometer
actions.body: Use a ThermoPop 2 immersion probe. Check it in a well-stirred ice-water slurry before the session. Keep the same glass and recorded fill mark.

actions.title: Read at the same point in the test
actions.body: Disable flavor through the normal controls. After the chosen idle, take the first sample and put the probe tip in mid-water as soon as the pour ends. Record when stable.

actions.title: Repeat at the selected cadence
actions.body: Record each successive pour, volume and temperature, then how long the unit takes to recover. This tests delivered water separately from the wall reading.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Save the first and successive water temperatures, sample conditions and recovery time.

pages.title: Decide the next gram
pages.subtitle: Read the water and refrigerant measurements together before changing the weighed charge.

drawing.value: Water load passes and inlet vapor margin holds
Keep the current fill and repeat.
Warm outlet, high superheat, slow cooling
Verify limits, airflow and leaks first.
or a distinct temperature drop at the drier
Cold coil with poor water cooling
Check fill, ice and wrap contact.
Inlet superheat near zero or liquid return
When excess is confirmed, recover and weigh back 1.0 g less.

actions.title: Change one measured variable
actions.body: Use a weighed 1.0 g step only when the actual evidence points to inventory and the service limits permit it. Keep capillary, instruments, airflow and load fixed.

actions.title: Test for a repeatable response
actions.body: Compare the same wall window and delivered-water readings. An addition should help cooling and reduce outlet superheat with the inlet margin intact. Diagnose before a second addition.

actions.title: Keep a passing charge
actions.body: Keep the weighed amount if the repeat tests meet the water duty and preserve inlet margin at the cold end and restart. Recover and weigh a smaller fill only if excess is established.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: Stop for near-zero inlet vapor margin, leak indication, lost airflow, overload or repeated trips.

pages.title: Read the cold controls in service
pages.subtitle: Use status and the physical fan, coil and water readings to verify what stops and restarts the unit.

drawing.value: Record a freeze stop if seen.
Freeze and faults may stop sooner.
Cold output parks if probe goes stale.

actions.title: Read status with real inputs
actions.body: Record wall and coil temperatures, relay state, hold and faults. Mark normal wall cutoff and any other stop in the log. Check the actual fan as the compressor cycles.

actions.title: Repeat the normal water sequence
actions.body: Use the matched pull-down and the same dispense and refill cadence. Confirm cooling recovers and restart honors the guard after a normal stop.

actions.title: Record what the first unit proves
actions.body: Save the measured charge, lowest inlet superheat, wall timing and delivered water results. Confirm final sealed access before treating the installed run as complete.

result.title: DONE WHEN
result.body: The trace shows the actual guard behavior, repeatable load response and final closure check.

pages.title: Repair through the full sequence
pages.subtitle: Recover the charge, clear residual gas and repeat the repair, leak test and weighed fill.

drawing.value: Clear residual gas and prove flow
Pressure test and log the vacuum hold
Weigh the net mass to the loop
A charged or leaking circuit never goes directly to heat.

actions.title: Isolate and identify the repair
actions.body: End the run from the safe disconnect. Record the leaking seam and the pressure state. An ambient alarm calls for the work-area protocol first.

actions.title: Recover and clear before opening
actions.body: Use the qualified A3 equipment and confirm residual clearance. Restore the verified inert sweep and heat protection for the repaired path.

actions.title: Repeat the recorded service sequence
actions.body: Repeat the inert pressure test, vacuum and net fill. Sweep the repaired seam and every disturbed fitting under the matching pressure state, then repeat the load check.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: A new pressure-test, vacuum, charge and leak record closes the repair.

pages.title: Save the checks with the unit
pages.subtitle: Keep the measurements that let the next run repeat the same conditions.

drawing.value: Model, compressor plate, leads, collar and mount photos.
Purge route, pressure/temperature hold and vacuum trace.
Scale check, fixture change, net charge and uncertainty.
Location, detector and reference response, pressure state.
Wall time, A/B/C readings if fitted, A/W, water in glass,
cutoff and restart, final sealed closure and recheck.

actions.title: Name each run
actions.body: Record unit, date, gauge and probe locations, instrument IDs, charge and bench definition. Keep the comparison rows for each candidate, including guard trips.

actions.title: Attach accessible and buried checks
actions.body: Save the pre-foam evidence, cooled joint photos and leak worksheet. Mark results for hidden parts with the whole-loop pressure-test record.

actions.title: Leave a repeatable final result
actions.body: Record the charge, acceptable water performance and lowest observed inlet margin. Include the final closure method and its leak result.

result.title: CHECK
result.body: The unit carries the measured charge, the acceptance trace and the completed service record.
